critical.issue: The dedicated 'boss' action is MISSING from BIOME_ACTIONS for every boss biome (ashen_border, demonfall_crater, diplomats_highlands, deep_forges, starfall_cliffs, ancient_den, abyssal_trench, elderroot_hollow). GET /game/data/biome/ashen_border/actions returns ['loot_ruins','hunt','gather']. POST /game/action {action_id:'boss', biome_id:'ashen_border', target_id:'boss_ashen_lord'} returns 400 'Action "boss" not available in biome "ashen_border"'. Bosses ARE reachable via 'hunt' (they were appended to hunt.targets), but the Phase-G spec explicitly requires a dedicated 'boss' action entry. ROOT CAUSE: in /app/backend/game_data.py the Phase-G boss-injection block (lines ~479-497) writes BIOME_ACTIONS[boss_biome].append({'id':'boss', ...}), but the subsequent _apply_biome_id_migration() at line 530 rebuilds BIOME_ACTIONS by iterating the old dict and remapping legacy keys (old_ruins→ashen_border etc.) — the old-key entries come after the new-key entries in insertion order and overwrite them, wiping out the boss action. FIX: either (a) move _apply_biome_id_migration() to run BEFORE the Phase-G injection, or (b) have the migration merge lists rather than overwrite on collision.

rca of the issue: BIOME_ACTIONS boss-action bug — In /app/backend/game_data.py the Phase-G injection loop (added at lines ~479-497) mutates BIOME_ACTIONS in place, appending a `{id:'boss', name:'Boss', targets:[boss_id]}` entry to the canonical-key list (e.g. BIOME_ACTIONS['ashen_border']). Immediately afterward, _apply_biome_id_migration() rebuilds BIOME_ACTIONS by walking (k,v) pairs and re-keying legacy names via BIOME_ID_MAP. Because both the legacy key (`old_ruins`) and the canon key (`ashen_border`) exist by that point (extend_world_data pre-populated the canon key), the migration processes them sequentially and, with dict-insertion order, the legacy `old_ruins`→`ashen_border` remap OVERWRITES the just-injected canon list that contained the boss entry. Fix: run migration once, then inject; OR use `remapped.setdefault(new_k, []).extend(v)` for list-typed values. Verified fix would work by reproducing in isolation (see agent trace) — direct Phase-G injection into a clean dict does produce the expected `['loot_ruins','hunt','gather','boss']` list. Symptom: dedicated 'boss' action UI target is unavailable; players can still fight bosses via 'hunt' because hunt.targets was extended in the same block and hunt.targets survives the migration overwrite because extend_world_data's canonical `hunt` entry already contained the hunt-target mutation before the migration ran.
